items.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: all the arrangements he did for Tony Bennett of course

ctx.x: Well we’ll have to do another part.

One thing I’d like to add, Utica really outdid itself so to speak in the amount of talent that both resided there and came from there, just in the area of music. Whether it’s John Simonelli, who I think became the first chair hornist with the Philadelphia who played under Mason Jones. We played in all city high school band together. I could tell he was great then. He had an incredible sound on the French horn. He used to walk around rehearsal room before we started band rehearsal playing [scats] like that. I knew…
